source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-58: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 58 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
For Mooncake variant 58, treat disaggregated KV serving as an environment-dependent hypothesis, not a guaranteed improvement. Assume a multi-node long-context service, but first inventory model and runtime versions, GPU/NIC models, PCIe/NUMA affinity, link rate, memory limits, failure domains, prompt and generation-length distributions, concurrency, batching, and authorization boundaries. Unknown platform facts remain unknown.

The measurement and attribution plan must separate prefill workers, which construct KV, from decode workers, which consume it. Specify KV block format and precision, ownership and placement, replication, TTL and eviction priority, cache-key tenant isolation, version/checksum validation, admission quotas, batching, migration, and control-plane behavior. Reject stale, partial, unauthorized, or checksum-failing blocks; on a miss or failed transfer use a bounded local/recompute fallback rather than unverified data.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at a pre-registered offered load and fixed workload mix, remote KV lowers decode time-to-first-token or GPU memory pressure versus a matched local-KV and conventional distributed baseline without increasing p95/p99 end-to-end latency, error rate, or isolation failures beyond pre-set margins. Measure TTFT, inter-token latency, end-to-end latency, throughput, queue time, KV hit/miss and eviction rates, bytes and RDMA read/write latency, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, retries, and recovery time. Use synchronized timestamps, units, percentiles, repeated trials, confidence intervals, warm-up separation, and controlled prompt lengths, batching, concurrency, placement, and model versions; attribute transfer, queueing, compute, and fallback separately.

Before rollout, run read-only checks and authorized fault tests for stale blocks, cache/node/link/control-plane loss, partial writes, timeout, and retry storms. Record correctness and tenant-isolation checks. Roll back or disable remote KV if p99 latency, error rate, stale/invalid block detection, isolation, or recovery-time thresholds are exceeded; preserve bounded fallback and audit logs. Do not claim a gain without the matched baselines and telemetry above.
